verses.text: Dare any of you, having a matter against his neighbor, go to law before the unrighteous, and not before the saints?
Don’t you know that the saints will judge the world? And if the world is judged by you, are you unworthy to judge the smallest matters?
Don’t you know that we will judge angels? How much more, things that pertain to this life?
If then, you have to judge things pertaining to this life, do you set them to judge who are of no account in the assembly?
I say this to move you to shame. Isn’t there even one wise man among you who would be able to decide between his brothers?
But brother goes to law with brother, and that before unbelievers!
Therefore it is already altogether a defect in you, that you have lawsuits one with another. Why not rather be wronged? Why not rather be defrauded?
No, but you yourselves do wrong, and defraud, and that against your brothers.
Or don’t you know that the unrighteous will not inherit God’s Kingdom? Don’t be deceived. Neither the sexually immoral, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor male prostitutes, nor homosexuals,
nor thieves, nor covetous, nor drunkards, nor slanderers, nor extortionists, will inherit God’s Kingdom.
Such were some of you, but you were washed. But you were sanctified. But you were justified in the name of the Lord Jesus, and in the Spirit of our God.
“All things are lawful for me,” but not all things are expedient. “All things are lawful for me,” but I will not be brought under the power of anything.
“Foods for the belly, and the belly for foods,” but God will bring to nothing both it and them. But the body is not for sexual immorality, but for the Lord; and the Lord for the body.
Now God raised up the Lord, and will also raise us up by his power.
Don’t you know that your bodies are members of Christ? Shall I then take the members of Christ, and make them members of a prostitute? May it never be!
Or don’t you know that he who is joined to a prostitute is one body? For, “The two”, he says, “will become one flesh.”
But he who is joined to the Lord is one spirit.
Flee sexual immorality! “Every sin that a man does is outside the body,” but he who commits sexual immorality sins against his own body.
Or don’t you know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit who is in you, whom you have from God? You are not your own,
for you were bought with a price. Therefore glorify God in your body and in your spirit, which are God’s.

footnotes.content: Paul sounds the alarm here—not against justice itself, but against believers running to pagan courts when they have the family to sort such things within. He's asking: why would you settle your dispute *outside* where Christ's people gather?
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: What a reversal of vision this is: the saints will one day judge the world, yet now shrink from settling a neighbor's quarrel. Paul is reminding them of their own dignity in Christ—the authority they have already been given.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: We will judge angels. Let that sink in. And yet you cannot judge a property dispute or a broken contract? Paul presses the absurdity—our *present* calling to walk in wisdom and discernment is a real thing, not a waiting game.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The jab lands gently. Paul asks: when you hand your disputes to pagan judges, what does it say about your trust in the people God has *given* you—those 'of no account' in the world's eyes, but beloved in the church?
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Paul speaks to shame—not to crush, but to wake. 'Isn't there even one wise man among you?' He's saying: you have what you need. The Holy Spirit dwells in you. Use the gifts you've been given to heal your own rifts.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The shame deepens: brother suing brother *before unbelievers*. Imagine the witness—the watching world sees not Christ's reconciliation, but His body at war with itself. What testimony does that give?
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Here is the knife-edge of Paul's teaching: better to suffer wrong than to drag the name of Jesus into a pagan courtroom. Better to lose money than lose the witness. The kingdom works by a strange math.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Paul turns the mirror: *you* are the ones doing the wronging and defrauding. Not the pagans, not the flesh—you, the brothers, the beloved. The problem isn't outside; it's here, inside the church.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Paul lists the acts that cut you off from God's kingdom—a sober catalog. But notice: he's not listing them to condemn the Corinthians. He's naming the life they've *left behind*, to remind them who they are now.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The list continues—thieves, drunkards, slanderers. Each one cuts at the fabric of trust and honor. Paul is saying: you know what these look like. You've seen the wreckage. Don't go back.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The great turning: 'Such were some of you.' Past tense. Washed, sanctified, justified—three gifts that have already remade you. When Paul sees the Corinthians, he sees people the blood of Jesus has already cleaned and set apart.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Paul quotes what sounds like Corinthian freedom talk: 'All things are lawful for me.' But he catches it—yes, lawful, but not all things build you up. There's a difference between what's permitted and what *serves* you.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Again they echo some slogan: 'Foods for the belly, and the belly for foods.' It's an argument for indifference—eat, it's natural, temporary. But Paul reframes: your body isn't a trash can; it belongs to the Lord.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God raised the Lord, and will raise us too—by the same power. That's the climax Paul is building toward. Your body isn't disposable; it's destined for resurrection. Treat it as something Christ has a claim on.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Paul's shock is real: your bodies are members of Christ. He's not saying your body is *like* a temple or *represents* Christ. He's saying you *are* Him, joined to Him as a body is joined to its head. How could you ever treat that lightly?
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Paul quotes Genesis 2:24—the words said at the first wedding, where two become one flesh. Sexual union isn't casual; it's the deepest of joinings, meant to reflect that primal covenant. When you join yourself to someone outside Christ's body, the joining itself speaks.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: But he who is joined to the Lord is one spirit. Readers today hear an echo in this—many have felt the loneliness of choosing the Lord when a world offers itself in other embraces. Yet Paul promises that union with Christ fills something no other joining can reach.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: 'Flee sexual immorality'—the only sin Paul tells us to *run from*. He doesn't say argue about it or study it or manage it. Flee. Because it harms your own body in a way other sins don't; it breaks the unity you're being grafted into.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit. Not was. *Is*. Right now, in whatever shape you're in, whatever you've done—the Spirit indwells you. That's the reality Paul keeps pressing. You belong to God; your body isn't yours to squander.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: You were bought with a price—the blood of Christ. This settles it. Your freedom isn't freedom from constraint; it's freedom *purchased* at infinite cost, for a purpose: to glorify God with your whole self, body and spirit together.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
